features.name: Reactions: when this happens, do that
features.what: The world notices what the player does (a kill, a read note, an arrival) and answers in small, readable ways.

features.name: One button for everything
features.what: F, Space, Enter or one button talks, opens, trades, goes through doors and starts a fight; it also turns note pages and closes speech. E answers to the same verb as an unadvertised alias.

features.name: A quiet, uncluttered screen, WASD and a calm step
features.what: The how-to-move line goes after your first step, fight buttons show only near a monster, messages sit in a small corner panel, Interact is the one big button with four small icon buttons beside it, Dusk and Dawn live in the Menu, WASD walks, and Trade closes with F.

features.name: Levels, or learning by doing
features.what: The hero grows: experience and levels (classic), or skills that improve with use.

features.name: Monsters and cozy fights
features.what: Monsters with health and bite, bump to strike, and a way to lose that never ends the game.

features.name: Books and notes you find
features.what: Notes, letters and books lying in the world, in chests, or given by people; kept and re-readable.

features.name: Items, a bag and a shop
features.what: Things to find, carry, use, buy and sell, including keep-forever tools.

features.name: Fog of war
features.what: Floors are dark until you walk them, and the map remembers what you saw.

features.name: Generated floors (drawn at build time)
features.what: `vefr delve` draws connected dungeon floors from a seed and wires their stairs.

features.name: publish, look and probe
features.what: Developer verbs: post a build to the gallery, screenshot the game and list text over the map, fire story events and read why they happened.

features.name: A game's interface as pictures
features.what: A folder of pictures inside a pack paints the buttons, panels, bars and cursor in the game's own look; high-contrast and forced-colour modes keep the plain style.

features.name: A new descent every run
features.what: The shared generator is built (the same floors in Python and in the browser); drawing a fresh descent each run in the game is still to come.

features.name: Rule saves
features.what: An optional per-pack setting so a reload keeps what the rules have done: fired rules, flags, beliefs and items.

features.name: Locks, keys and guardians
features.what: A door or stair locked behind a key item or a flag (built); a ladder of key-carrying guardians ending at the act's boss (proposed).

features.name: The album
features.what: One record of what you have met and found, and a sticker album that fills in as you play.

features.name: Gear in five slots
features.what: An item may name a slot and the atk and hp it changes; the Bag's 'You' section lets the hero wear and take off gear, with one plain sentence for every change.

features.name: A story in acts
features.what: One act ends and the next begins, with its own map and mood.

features.name: Starter art: themes, items and icons
features.what: 13 themed kits (tiles, items, characters), the delve icons (gear, spell schools, shop signs, item badges), the surface tiles and the full sticker set, at game size and credited.

features.name: A Blueprint for repeated monster families
features.what: An optional file at a pack root that expands a small family source into the region enemy records at build time. A pack without one is unchanged.

features.name: Small sounds
features.what: A few soft synthesized sounds for the moments of play, off with one switch.

features.name: Lamplight
features.what: Real light over the drawn map: darkness per phase, a light the hero carries, lamps that shine while a rule flag is set, and standing tiles that cast shadows; off with one switch.

features.name: A character that walks
features.what: An optional sprite sheet beside a sprite gives it a walk cycle: idle when standing, one frame per step, and a missing side mirrored.

features.name: One portable .vefr file for a game
features.what: `vefr archive` writes a game as one ZIP: the pack's content, its pictures and sounds, and a versioned manifest with a digest per file. The shared Player opens it offline (open the two files together, or drop the .vefr on the Player); `vefr weave`'s self-contained HTML is unchanged beside it. Every load validates names (no path named twice), sizes, digests, URLs and the manifest schema before a byte of the game reaches the player.

features.name: Damage types, resistances and burning
features.what: A pack may opt in to typed damage: the hero's own resistances and immunities, and a hazard that deals a damage type and leaves the hero burning for a count of turns. A pack that declares none of it deals the same untyped blows as before (built for one status effect; hazards authored in a Blueprint, and resistances granted by worn gear, are still to come).

features.name: The RPG core: rolls, guard, depth, spoils, stock, traits, magic and trips
features.what: A pack may opt in, key by key, to rolled blows (misses and critical hits) and a turn for every drink or cast; guard on the hero, worn gear and monsters; a Section's curve read at play; a family's drop chance and gold; a shop's own stock and markup; a traits table whose words change numbers, react and curse, worn or carried in a bag; mana for learned spells and charges for things that cast; and a descent that resumes at the deepest landing, a fall that wakes at home with the bag left where the hero fell, and a rest that heals. A pack that names none of it plays exactly as before.
